manifest.name: dsh-plugin-local-infer
manifest.description: DeepSeek Harness plugin that manages local inference engines (llama.cpp, NInfer, Hyper-Qwen, Strata): configure, size, launch, and publish a local engine as a DSH model. Installable bundle that mounts the localInfer service, engine providers, model-facing tools, and the Web UI as one profile layer.

bundle.text:
# The dsh-plugin-local-infer bundle patch: mounts the whole local-inference
# capability as ONE layer over an existing dsh profile.
#
# Row order carries no load semantics — activation is service-availability
# driven — so the seam may appear before or after the providers that fill it.
# The user's own profile patch layer can address any row below by `id` to
# retune it (last write per row wins).

- insert:
    # Client carrier: mounts the bare package name so the client-module scan
    # keys the `dsh.client` declaration on it and loads dsh/client.js (the
    # browser "Engine settings" card) into the boot graph. The scan only maps
    # a bare package-root entry to its `dsh.client` field, never a subpath, so
    # this row is what makes the client half reachable. The host module is a
    # no-op; the capability lives in the four subpath rows below.
    - id: local-infer
      name: 'dsh-plugin-local-infer'

    # Service Definition: publishes ctx.localInfer, the engine/preset/guideline
    # registries, and the orchestration entry points (estimate, guidelines,
    # deps, installString, runInstall, launch, registerModel). Carries no store
    # of its own.
    - id: local-infer-service
      name: 'dsh-plugin-local-infer/service'

    # Service Providers: the concrete engine adapters (ninfer, hyperqwen,
    # llamacpp, strata), the NInfer VramModel, the built-in presets, the
    # built-in guidelines, and the per-OS SystemDep install command data. Each
    # registers itself with ctx.localInfer.
    - id: local-infer-providers
      name: 'dsh-plugin-local-infer/providers'

    # Consumer: the model-facing local_infer_* tools (estimate, launch, status,
    # register), their system-prompt section, and their per-tool timeout budgets.
    - id: local-infer-tool
      name: 'dsh-plugin-local-infer/tool'

    # Web UI: the parameter form (form-type aware), the VRAM meter, the
    # red-warning banner, the engine lifecycle controls, and the register-as-
    # model confirmation.
    - id: local-infer-ui
      name: 'dsh-plugin-local-infer/ui'

    # Orchestrator: the opt-in "Orchestrator" card and its system-prompt
    # injection. Ships disabled: the Plugins page Components toggle writes the
    # enabling override in the user's profile patch layer.
    - id: local-infer-orchestrator
      name: 'dsh-plugin-local-infer/orchestrator'
      disabled: true

readme.text:
[中文 (Chinese)](docs/zh/README.md)

> For those who want more performance out of their specific hardware than what Unsloth gives out of the box.

[](https://github.com/cybtachyon/dsh-plugin-local-infer/blob/main/LICENSE)
[](https://www.npmjs.com/package/@deepseek-ai/dsh)
[](https://github.com/topics/dsh-plugin)

A DeepSeek Harness plugin that manages local inference engines:

- llama.cpp
- NInfer
- Hyper-Qwen (vLLM)
- Infernix
- Strata
- ...with more coming soon.

Pick a model and an engine, tune the parameters, watch a live **VRAM Est.** meter, see **hardware warnings** the moment a value (or a parameter itself) is unsafe for the detected hardware, then the plugin manages **build, deploy, and health-check** for each engine and **automatically register it as a DSH model** once it is confirmed working. No hand-editing of finicky yaml or launchers.

dsh plugin --profile web add https://github.com/cybtachyon/dsh-plugin-local-infer
```

When installing from a local checkout, run `pnpm build` first: it type-checks
the workspace (`tsc -b`) and then produces the `dsh/client.js` browser card
artifact with esbuild (`node scripts/build-client.mjs`).

Web UI: click **Plugins** → **Add Plugin** → paste `dsh-plugin-local-infer`.

Or add from the DSH Plugin Marketplace.
The **Engine settings** card mounts on the Plugins page (older hosts: the Settings page).

- **Pick an engine and model**, then tune the parameters. Each field renders by its type: checkboxes, dropdowns, sliders, text, directory pickers, and a chat-template combo (known templates plus free text).
- **Watch the VRAM Est. meter.** It prices weights, KV cache, overhead, and workspace against your card as you adjust values, and shows the verdict (`fits` / `tight` / `over`) and the largest context that fits.
- **Read the warnings.** Red banners and inline field warnings fire when a parameter value, or the presence of a parameter, is unsafe for your detected hardware.
- **Satisfy the system dependencies.** The panel lists each missing host dependency (docker, CUDA toolkit, ffmpeg, hf CLI, ...) with its purpose, a copy/paste install string for your OS, and an optional one-click **Run** (sudo). The **Get** button stays disabled until every dependency reports satisfied.
- **Get.** With the dependencies satisfied, `Get` syncs the engine's source: it clones the engine's git repo (or the **Engine Fork** you provided) into the **Engine Directory** override, or with no override into the engine default checkout home `~/.cache/dsh/infer/<engine>` (one checkout per engine, derived at run

When a parameter can be set both as a CLI argument and as a write to the engine's config file, the plugin prefers the CLI argument. The CLI arg is consumed for that launch only, so it leaves the on-disk config file (and any customization you made by hand in it) untouched where possible.

All values persist to `~/.dsh/local-infer/config.json`; the browser never sees a value it did not store.

A **Get** or **Launch** that must run `sudo` first checks whether sudo credentials are cached. When they are not, both Launch buttons read **Sudo needed** (painted as a warning) and the line `Check your CLI for a sudo prompt` appears in the **Logs** section and the run's log file: the password prompt lands on the terminal that launched the harness, not in the browser. Type the password there. Without one within 60 seconds the run is killed and fails through the normal error path, and the buttons switch to **Logs**.

Local models often struggle with agentic workflows and can't "one-shot" prompts without assistance. The included **Orchestrator** package gives your model a default prompt that enables that capability.

- **Enable it** on the DeepSeek Harness **Plugins** page: open this plugin's entry and flip the **Orchestrator** component toggle (the component ships disabled). After first enabling the component, restart the host so it loads.
- **Edit the prompt** on the **Orchestrator** card that then appears: change the **Orchestrator Prompt** field and press **Save**. The default text ships in the plugin's `prompt.md`; clear the field and save to restore it.
- **It injects while enabled.** With the component enabled, the saved prompt is part of the agent's system prompt for new requests. A Save reaches the next request; no restart is needed after Save.
The saved prompt persists to `~/.dsh/local-infer/orchestrator.json`, beside the engine config.

| OS                           | State     | Notes                                                                                                               |
|------------------------------|-----------|---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------|
| Linux (Debian/Ubuntu, `apt`) | Supported | Install blocks mirror the working NInfer launcher: the CUDA keyring sequence plus the compile toolchain.            |
| Linux (Arch, `pacman`)       | Supported | `pacman` blocks plus the `/opt/cuda` export lines.                                                                  |
| Linux (Fedora, `dnf`)        | Untested  | Command set present, flagged untested on a live host.                                                               |
| macOS (`brew`)               | Partial   | CPU/docker path (llama.cpp). No NVIDIA Container Toolkit on macOS, so the CUDA engines' docker path is unavailable. |
| Windows (WSL2)               | Untested  | WSL2 is detected and the dflash2 pin-memory rule fires; the command set is flagged untested.                        |
| Windows                      | Partial   | Code paths are

| Engine            | Docker        | Local build        | State                                                                        |
|-------------------|---------------|--------------------|------------------------------------------------------------------------------|
| NInfer            | Yes           | Yes (cmake + CUDA) | The reference engine. Measured VRAM models for the Qwen 27B/35B artifacts.   |
| Hyper-Qwen (vLLM) | Yes (compose) | No                 | `.env`-driven docker-compose profiles.                                       |
| vLLM              | No            | No                 | Work-in-progress.                                                            |
| llama.cpp         | Yes           | Yes                | Specified, not verified until the binary is available.                       |
| Infernix          | No            | Yes (cmake + CUDA) | C++/CUDA fork of NInfer tuned for Qwen models on a single RTX 50-series GPU. Local build only. |
| Strata            | Yes           | No                 | Placeholder engine; its parameter surface is empty until the flag set lands. |
Runtime requirements: Node `^22.19.0 || >=24.0.0`, pnpm 12.11.2 (pinned by `mise.toml`), and the `@deepseek-ai/cordis >= 4.0.6-alpha.2` peer dependency.

What each common machine gets you in practice. Capability impressions are sourced from [r/LocalLLaMA](https://www.reddit.com/r/LocalLLaMA/) user threads. "Shared" means unified memory (the model and the OS share the pool).

| Hardware                        | Memory          | What you get                                                                                                                                                                  |
| ------------------------------- | --------------- | ----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| NVIDIA RTX 5090                 | 32 GB VRAM      | Reliably fits model weights up to 23 GB with 240k+ context and vision. Handles complex coding and vision tasks, but needs special tooling for very long or complex tasks.     |
| NVIDIA RTX 4090                 | 24 GB VRAM      | The community workhorse. 30B-class models fit at Q4 and drive coding agents; 70B needs slow CPU offload. Best speed-per-dollar single card.                                   |
| NVIDIA RTX 3090                 | 24 GB VRAM      | The used-card value king. Same 24 GB as a 4090 but an older generation: 32B at Q4 with modest context, no FP8. A single card is limiting; the common advice is to pair two.   |
| NVIDIA RTX PRO 6000             | 96 GB VRAM
